doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Joining Ellington after Harry Carney's funeral
summary: John Gensel asked him to play Sophisticated Lady at Harry Carney's funeral, and weeks later he was in the band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: That’s great. 1974 was a pretty significant year for the Ellington—

Yes. That’s when I went with the Ellington band, yes. That came about with John Gensel, the pastor at the Lutheran Church on 54th Street and Lexington Avenue. He was the Shepherd of the Night Flocks, he was the pastor for the jazz community, John Gensel. He asked me to play at Harry Carney’s funeral. So I played “Sophisticated Lady” at Harry’s funeral. Harry was a good friend of mine too. And that’s how that came about. A few weeks later I was in the band.
